headings: Why the Same Alarm Feels Different
attempts.raw_text:
### Why the Same Alarm Feels Different

As the night progresses, sleep normally shifts from more deep slow-wave sleep toward lighter NREM and REM sleep. If an alarm—or a natural awakening—catches deep N3 sleep, waking may be harder and groggier. From lighter sleep, the same scheduled moment may feel easier, without requiring prediction of the exact minute.

### A Habit Some People Develop

This ability may also reflect a learned routine, not a universal human trait. In an 11-person home study, self-awakening success reached 82% on day seven after a week of trying. Separately, 66 of 643 students—10.3%—reported a daily habit and kept schedules about 30 minutes earlier, an association with morningness. Practice may matter, though causation remains unproven.

## In one line

Waking before the alarm may be less a superpower than a quiet meeting point between sleep depth, personal timing, and routine.
